title: A Verifier Taxonomy and Open Benchmark for Detectability of LLM‑Generated NetOps Failures
abstract: We preregistered, executed, and analysed a paired confirmatory study (cnd-2026-004-prereg-v1) that tested whether a machine‑readable verifier taxonomy plus a seeded NetOps task bank yields measurable marginal detectability when a guarded verifier (syntax+policy+reachability+stateful) replaces a syntax‑only baseline. Using gpt-5-mini with a single shared initial candidate per task (100 shared calls), each candidate was deterministically scored by (a) a syntax baseline and (b) a guarded layered verifier. On the preregistered confirmatory set (N=100 paired tasks) both verifiers validated every candidate (baseline = 100/100; guarded = 100/100), producing a ceiling result (paired difference = 0.00, 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0). The saturation prevents evaluation of the preregistered ≥15 percentage‑point effect but yields artifact‑grounded lessons about task‑bank design, shared‑generation protocols, and practical verifier audit value. All execution, scorer traces, responses, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for deterministic reproducibility (see Disclosure Statement).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are rapidly proposed for NetOps tasks—intent→configuration translation, change planning, and remediation. Operational adoption requires deterministic audit gates that convert probabilistic candidates into audited change proposals (example verifier classes: syntax, policy/workflow, reachability, stateful emulation). We preregistered a controlled empirical test (cnd-2026-004-prereg-v1) to measure whether upgrading a lightweight syntax verifier to a guarded layered verifier increases the fraction of candidates that deterministic oracles reject (i.e., increases detectability). Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact‑hashed paired within‑task experiment comparing syntax vs. guarded verifiers on 100 seeded NetOps tasks; (2) an archived, deterministic execution bundle (model calls, provider traces, responses, scoring JSONs, task manifests) enabling exact reproduction; and (3) operational lessons about where verifier stacks provide practical value and how benchmark design shapes measurable marginal gains. The final research question: Does a stronger layered verifier yield higher deterministic detectability than a syntax-only verifier on a seeded NetOps confirmatory bank?
sections.related_work: Prior work provides deterministic verification and synthesis foundations (Minesweeper, Propane, Batfish, Plankton) and demonstrates generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines for code/IaC. Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations and IaC error taxonomies describe mechanical vs. semantic failure classes and argue for verifier‑assisted pipelines. Our study differs by preregistering the estimand, using a paired within‑task design, and releasing a complete deterministic artifact bundle so that claims and numeric outcomes are directly traceable to archived JSON scoring records.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration (cnd-2026-004-prereg-v1; SHA‑256: e4c20e24f495a61d4e25292a06ab488a31a1c5672309f9db56a26693ec6cec7c) specified a paired design (N=100 paired tasks) and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (within‑task difference in binary detection). Sampling, inclusion/exclusion, stopping rules, seeds, and deterministic analysis were fixed there.
Generation and orchestration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The published execution used a shared_initial protocol: one LLM call per task produced a single candidate that both verifiers independently scored (execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/responses/*.txt archive every call and response; representative provider call: execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json, SHA‑256 c7ee45af524e249534c47489c1c46e2d6143bda1475489529fe9cbb8b04ddc91). The preregistration fixed independent_condition_generation=false (one shared candidate per task) and the exact binary detection mapping.
Verifier exemplars and scoring rule (deterministic and archived). Two deterministic verifier exemplars were archived and used without human adjudication: (A) baseline syntax-only exemplar (command grammar and CLI-format checks) and (B) guarded layered exemplar (syntax + policy/workflow constraint checks + symbolic reachability/final‑state comparison + stateful emulation). Both are implemented in the archived scorer instance deterministic_netops_validator_v5; all per-episode scoring JSONs are archived at execution/scoring/*.json. The preregistered binary mapping is applied exactly and deterministically: detected = 1 iff scoring_status == "COMPLETED" AND score == 1 AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true; otherwise detected = 0. This rule is implemented in the scoring artifacts (see execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json examples).
Task bank and provenance. The confirmatory bank used 100 synthetic tasks generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task manifest entry contains task_payload fields (intent, required_sequence, workflow_policies, difficulty.level). The authoritative task manifest is execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: cc2ec3b065310cc471c9d1842b88450d05b2a21802cda775083b88f856003848). Inclusion/exclusion rules (public provenance, contamination checks, deterministic re-seeding) were applied by the harness and logged.
Analysis plan. Primary analysis: paired comparison using exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for a 95% CI on the paired difference. Technical/infrastructure failures are handled per preregistration (they are excluded from the primary analysis; sensitivity rules archived). All analysis code and outputs are archived (analysis/*).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The harness completed 200 episodes (100 paired tasks), consumed 100 model calls (model_calls_used = 100; maximum_model_calls = 200), recorded zero infrastructure failures, and produced reconciled artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json; deterministic reconciliation artifact hashed and archived).
Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑grounded, exact):
- baseline_success_count = 100 / 100 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0)
- guarded_success_count = 100 / 100 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0)
- paired contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00) = (100, 0, 0, 0) (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256 a2fcb23845ebf1813786132ad133a0616fa4e58db48dc2eb2914b276910b49d1)
- paired estimate = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; seed = 1729)
- McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0.
Representative, inspectable artifacts (examples cited with authoritative SHA‑256s):
- pair-000001: shared response execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...), scoring JSONs execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256 e431d77d...) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256 45a30296...).
- pair-000002 and pair-000003 analogous representative artifacts are archived (see execution_manifest for full per-episode paths and SHA‑256s). The full response SHA manifest shows the baseline and guarded condition responses are byte‑identical per task (explaining the absence of discordant pairs). All listed paths and SHA‑256 checksums are authoritative and archived.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The preregistered hypothesis expected a measurable positive marginal detectability of the guarded verifier over the syntax baseline (≥15 percentage points). The run produced saturation: both verifiers validated every shared candidate in the confirmatory bank (100/100 each). This ceiling outcome is artifact‑grounded and yields three lessons: (1) many engineered confirmatory tasks contain explicit mechanical signals (syntax, ordering, required shutdown/restore sequences) that syntax validators already catch, (2) richer verifier stacks materially increase audit traceability (validator_trace contains final_state, parsed_command_count, touched_field counts) but may not change the binary accept/reject outcome on such banks, and (3) measuring marginal verifier value requires benchmark banks emphasising non‑syntactic semantic/intent failures and multi‑draw generation per task to expose stochastic divergences.
Reviewer‑requested clarifications added here (artifact‑grounded). Reviewers asked for (A) a compact per‑leaf taxonomy summary. The authoritative taxonomy labels are stored in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 cc2ec3b0...). Because that manifest is the single source of truth for per‑task taxonomy labels, we provide the manifest path and SHA so exact leaf counts can be deterministically computed from the archive. We do not transcribe manifest counts in prose to avoid transcription error—consumers should derive exact per‑leaf counts from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (path and SHA cited). (B) A clear statement that the shared_initial generation protocol (one identical candidate per task) deterministically reduces opportunities for discordant accept/reject outcomes: the harness generated one shared candidate per task and both verifiers scored the same candidate (see execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json, SHA‑256 c7ee45af... and the full response SHA manifest). That design choice is preregistered and explains the degenerate McNemar table (n10=n01=0). We added an explicit Methods sentence describing this effect and its statistical consequence (a saturated contingency table yields degenerate CI and an uninformative McNemar p-value). (C) The shared_initial generation prompt and its provenance are archived: exact provider call payloads are at execution/provider_calls/*.json (representative file execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json, SHA‑256 c7ee45af524e2495...). The archivally authoritative prompt and provider trace are thus available for exact reproduction; we include the authoritative path and SHA rather than transcribing the provider_call JSON here to preserve an exact provenance link.
Operational implications and future work. For pipelines where expected failures are mechanically manifest, lightweight validators can detect the majority of incorrect proposals at lower cost than full emulation. For intent/semantic mismatch failures, layered verifiers, adversarial test banks, human oversight, and multiple-generation draws remain necessary. We encourage future evaluations to (1) construct task banks that emphasise non‑syntactic/ambiguous intents, (2) use multiple independent generation draws per task, and (3) measure verifier marginality with a design that allows discordant outcomes (independent_condition_generation = true) so McNemar tests are informative.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment comparing a syntax-only baseline to a guarded layered verifier on a 100-item seeded NetOps confirmatory bank. Both verifiers validated every shared candidate (100/100), producing a saturated result that prevents evaluation of the preregistered effect size. The artifact bundle (model calls, provider traces, responses, scoring JSONs, task manifest, analysis outputs) is released to enable follow-up studies. Practical takeaway: verifier stacks improve auditability and trace richness, but measurable marginal detection gains require benchmarks and generation protocols that stress semantic/intent failure modes and stochastic generation variability.

limitations: Single model and shared‑generation protocol: we used gpt-5-mini with one shared candidate per task—this design (independent_condition_generation=false) deterministically reduces the opportunity for discordant accept/reject outcomes and contributed to the observed saturation; results therefore do not bound multi-draw or multi-model behaviour.
Synthetic confirmatory bank: the preregistered confirmatory set is synthetic and engineered; external validity to production operator proposals or adversarial semantic failures is limited.

Validator dependence: the measured construct "detected" depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5's scoring semantics and mapping; alternative validator implementations or different binary mappings could change numerical detection outcomes.
Ceiling/saturation: both conditions produced 100% detection on the confirmatory set, preventing inference regarding the preregistered effect size (≥15 percentage points).

Per‑leaf taxonomy counts: authoritative per‑task taxonomy labels are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 cc2ec3b065310cc471c9d1842b88450d05b2a21802cda775083b88f856003848); we provide this authoritative manifest path and SHA for deterministic per‑leaf counts rather than transcribing counts to avoid transcription errors.
